title: How to See the Orionid Meteor Shower and Other Upcoming Astronomical Events
gist: Wired Japan stargazing guide: the Orionid meteor shower peaks October 21-22 with up to 20 meteors per hour under dark skies, plus Saturn's opposition, a moon-Saturn pairing on October 24 and a moon-Pleiades pairing on October 27-28.

insights.claim: The Orionid meteor shower peaks October 21-22 in the US, with up to 20 meteors per hour in dark skies, and the best viewing is the early morning after moonset because the moon is about three-quarters full.
insights.speaker: Ritsuko Kawai
insights.so_what: Practical timing for viewers; no market relevance.
insights.locator: The Orionid meteor shower will be ongoing until November 7

insights.claim: The Orionids are fragments of Halley's Comet and are known for brightness and speed, sometimes producing fireballs as bright as Venus and glowing debris trains.
insights.speaker: Ritsuko Kawai
insights.so_what: Explains why the shower is a popular target.
insights.locator: these particular meteors are known for their brightness

insights.claim: Saturn reached opposition earlier this month, making it observable almost all night, and the moon passes close to it on October 24.
insights.speaker: Ritsuko Kawai
insights.so_what: Observing window for amateurs and researchers.
insights.locator: Earlier this month, Saturn reached opposition

insights.claim: Researchers recently found a decagon centered on Saturn's south pole, nearly half a century after the 18,600-mile-wide hexagon at the north pole, and the southern wave appears to be gaining momentum.
insights.speaker: Ritsuko Kawai
insights.so_what: Opposition gives scientists a closer look at the atmospheric waves believed to cause these structures.
insights.locator: a decagon centered on the planet’s south pole

insights.claim: The best view of the moon near the Pleiades is the evening of October 27 into the morning of October 28, when the cluster may be hard to see just after full moon without binoculars or a telescope.
insights.speaker: Ritsuko Kawai
insights.locator: The best time for viewing the Pleiades
